🚨 Mental Health Emergency

If you or your adolescent are experiencing a mental health emergency, please contact emergency services immediately:

  • Call 911 for immediate emergency assistance
  • National Suicide Prevention Lifeline: 988
  • Crisis Text Line: Text HOME to 741741
  • Go to your nearest emergency room

Do not wait or rely on information from this website during emergency situations.

Important Information

Educational Resource Only: This website provides educational information only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. We cannot provide individual medical recommendations or treatment advice.

Response Time: While we strive to respond to inquiries promptly, please allow several business days for a response. For urgent mental health concerns, please contact a qualified healthcare provider or emergency services.

Privacy: We respect your privacy and do not share contact information with third parties. Any feedback you provide may be used to improve our educational resources.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you recommend specific treatment providers or programs?

We are an educational resource and cannot make specific treatment recommendations. Our regional guides provide information about types of services available in different areas, but families should consult with qualified healthcare providers for personalized recommendations.

Can you provide medical advice about my adolescent's condition?

No, we cannot provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment recommendations. Please consult with qualified mental health professionals for guidance specific to your adolescent's needs.

How often is your content updated?

We regularly review and update our content to ensure accuracy and relevance. If you notice outdated information, please let us know so we can prioritize updates.

Can I share your resources with others?

Yes, our educational resources are designed to be shared with families, professionals, and community members who may find them helpful. We encourage sharing information that may benefit others navigating adolescent behavioral health challenges.

Do you provide services in languages other than English?

Currently, our content is available in English. We recognize the importance of multilingual resources and welcome feedback about language accessibility needs in the communities we serve.

Professional Resources and Partnerships

We welcome input from mental health professionals, educators, healthcare providers, and other professionals working with adolescents and families. Your expertise helps us ensure our educational content is accurate, relevant, and useful.

For Mental Health Professionals

If you are a mental health professional and have feedback about our content, suggestions for additional resources, or notice areas where information could be improved, we value your input.

For Educators and School Personnel

School-based professionals play a crucial role in supporting adolescent mental health. We welcome feedback about how our resources can better serve the educational community.

For Healthcare Providers

Primary care providers, pediatricians, and other healthcare professionals often serve as the first point of contact for families seeking mental health resources. Your perspective helps us create content that supports your work with families.

Community Feedback

Our resources are strengthened by input from the communities we serve. We welcome feedback from:

  • Families who have used our resources
  • Community organizations serving adolescents and families
  • Advocacy groups focused on mental health
  • Cultural and community leaders
  • Anyone working to improve adolescent behavioral health services

Your feedback helps us understand how our resources are being used and how we can improve them to better serve families and professionals.
